Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

August noun

classical

Juv. 3.9: Augustō … mēnse
Traupman 77

Augustus, Augusta, Augustum

adjective, with mēnsis; also a masculine noun (sc. mēnsis)

of August; August

Named after Augustus, who gave his name to Sextīlis rather than to September, the month of his birth, because his first consulship and his great victories fell in it (Suet. Aug. 31.2). Kalendae, Nōnae, Īdūs Augustae: the 1st, 5th and 13th.

Examples

  • Augustō recitantēs mēnse poētās

    poets giving readings in August (one of the horrors of Rome)Juv. 3.9

  • quīnque diēs tibi pollicitus mē rūre futūrum, Sextīlem tōtum mendāx dēsīderor

    I promised you I would be in the country five days, and I am missed the whole of August, a liarHor. Ep. 1.7.1–2

Other words

  • Sextīlis, Sextīle — August (the old name)

    adjective, with mēnsis; also a masculine noun (sc. mēnsis) · also used · classical · Hor. Ep. 1.7.2: Sextīlem tōtum; Cic. Att. 4.1.4: Nōnīs Sextīlibus; Traupman 78

    The sixth month, counting from March (sextus).

See also month, July, September, summer holidays.
